notes.text: Names Elazar ben Pedat and Elazar ben Shammua in the chain, via Shimon ben Elyakim.
Names Shimon ben Elyakim, ben Pedat, ben Shammua, and Elazar son of Shimon in distinct roles.
Elazar reports in ben Azaryah’s name.
The same chain also directly verifies that Sheshet reports in Elazar’s name.
Ammi explicitly reports in Elazar’s name.
Opening of seven sequential Elazar-in-Chanina reports at [15–21].
Elazar expressly transmits Yannai through Abbahu.
Elazar explicitly transmits Yishmael.
Resh Lakish shows Elazar a dinar.
Contains a separate Elazar report in Resh Lakish’s name, without a dinar. The next pass should separate these two English clauses and links.
Yonah and Ulla bar Yishmael are given immediately before “in the name of Rabbi Leazar.”
Back-reference to the named Chiyya evidence.
Back-reference to the discussion of Yochanan.
Back-reference. The earlier paragraph qualifies Rav as like his teacher.
Back-reference to exact Shmuel discussion.
Points to the list and competing second-Oshaya explanation.
Names Abbahu in the chain transmitting Elazar’s dispatch; provides example for Abbahu only.
The checked travel account names Rabbah bar bar Chana and uses the first-person plural. Preserve source name separately rather than silently identifying the roster’s Abba with him.
The matching episode is named explicitly above. Separate chronology and person identification.
Reciprocal reference to the discussion of Pedat and the Tosafot question.

Both Resh Lakish chains at [3,7] are transmitted by Il’a in this witness. Retain as a citation or name mismatch pending collation. Read the cited daf and neighboring context with the pinned digital text. Compare original editions before choosing an alternate target.

This address mentions Elazar and a rule about the red heifer. The pinned daf does not yield the stated Sheshet-to-Elazar chain. Hold the claimed witness. Read the cited daf and neighboring context with the pinned digital text. Compare original editions before choosing an alternate target.
The report is attributed to Yuchasin and immediately qualified by a nonfinding. Preserve the two voices. No exact question was located from the attribution and the work title alone.

The claimed encounter remains unlocated in the named chapter. Checked both the Guggenheimer digital chapter and the Mechon Mamre text for Huna/Huna bar Chinena/Chanina and likely forms with the two named parties.
The note points to Assi material but states no specific attribution here. Assi appears in the already linked appeasement, wedding and Chariot sources. Leave this roster occurrence bare.
No expansion or precise pointer is established. The already checked bar bar Chana episodes are a possible context, but the ending letter remains unsupported.
The roster gives a name and a generic pointer, with no relationship stated. No link is admitted without a definite reference and reciprocal passage.
The roster gives an ordainer omitted in the checked ordination episode. Ketubbot 112a names no ordainer. Preserve the roster claim without adopting an identity or imputing a missing source.

The sources establish named transmission; the roster additionally calls him a student. Chullin 7a, Zevachim 65b and Bekhorot 56a attest transmission or an exchange; retain the narrator’s relationship designation as a claim.
